topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: run conductor coverage against kona-node
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Enable the conductor acceptance suite to run against real `kona-node` sequencers, using the same behavioral requirements as op-node.

This depends on #21902, which tracks moving the broader conductor system coverage from `op-e2e` into `op-acceptance-tests`.

## Current state

The existing conductor acceptance test explicitly skips Kona:

- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/base/conductor/leadership_transfer_test.go`

The underlying preset is op-node-specific:

- `op-devstack/sysgo/singlechain_variants.go`
- `startConductorNode` accepts `*OpNode` and mutates op-node configuration directly.

The test under `rust/kona/tests/node/common/conductor_test.go` is also not real Kona coverage: `rust/kona/tests/node/utils/mixed_preset_with_conductor.go` delegates to the same op-node-only `presets.NewMinimalWithConductors` preset.

## Scope

### Devstack support

- Generalize conductor-managed CL setup around backend-neutral capabilities:
  - user RPC endpoint;
  - configure conductor RPC;
  - force stopped startup;
  - lifecycle/restart control.
- Preserve the existing op-node implementation.
- Add a `KonaNode` implementation using production CLI/RPC paths.
- Use stable RPC endpoints or TCP proxies to resolve the startup dependency between `kona-node` and `op-conductor` without reserving flaky fixed ports.
- Start all conductor-managed Kona sequencers stopped.
- Configure Kona's admin RPC, conductor RPC, L1/L2 endpoints, and P2P connectivity required by conductor health checks and failover.

### Shared acceptance coverage

Run the same conductor behavior tests against:

- op-node sequencers;
- Kona sequencers.

Do not add client-specific assertion branches. Product incompatibilities exposed by the shared suite should be fixed in Kona or tracked explicitly.

At minimum, Kona coverage should verify:

- cluster bootstrap with exactly one active sequencer;
- explicit leadership transfer and active-state handoff;
- continued block production and hash convergence after transfer;
- active sequencer failure and automatic failover;
- disaster-recovery override;
- conductor proxy behavior;
- unsafe payload commit fencing during conductor RPC failure.

### Kona compatibility likely exercised by the suite

Audit and test the Kona implementation for:

- conductor RPC timeout wiring;
- `conductor_overrideLeader` parameter compatibility;
- leadership and unsafe-head validation in `admin_startSequencer`;
- committing a payload to conductor before canonicalizing or gossiping it;
- handling ambiguous commit failures/timeouts without publishing an uncommitted payload.

Fast Rust integration tests should cover these internal invariants in addition to the full acceptance tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The conductor preset can launch a three-member conductor cluster backed by real `kona-node` processes.
- [ ] No conductor acceptance test skips based on `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node`.
- [ ] The shared suite passes against both op-node and Kona without client-specific assertion branches.
- [ ] CI has an explicit Kona conductor acceptance job or matrix entry that builds and runs the real Kona binary.
- [ ] The fixture asserts that its CL nodes are actually Kona, preventing silent fallback to op-node.
- [ ] Leadership handoff verifies active state, block progression, and hash convergence.
- [ ] Conductor commit failure cannot result in canonicalization or gossip of an uncommitted Kona payload.

## Related

- #21902
- #16418
- Archived upstream issues:
  - https://github.com/op-rs/kona/issues/3094
  - https://github.com/op-rs/kona/issues/3095

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: op-node and kona-node safedb parity
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473. Depends on #23475, #23476 and #23477 (the two RPCs and the flag that lets the devstack enable a kona-node safedb).

## Why

The RPC answers are the compatibility surface between the two implementations, and the byte layout is not (`docs/ai/safedb-review.md`). Consumers must not be able to tell an op-node from a kona-node behind `optimism_safeHeadAtL1Block` and `superroot_atTimestamp`. The only way to know that is to run both on the same chain and compare every answer, through the scenarios that have historically broken the record: resets, reorgs, restarts and resyncs.

## Shape

One acceptance package, `op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_parity`, on a `MixedSingleChainRuntime` with one sequencer plus two verifiers on the same L1 and L2: an op-node verifier and a kona-node verifier, both with a safedb path. op-node is the reference; its answers are the expected values. op-node itself is not changed by this work.

Scenarios, each ending with `VerifySafeHeadDatabaseMatches` in both directions over every recorded L1 block, plus a `superroot_atTimestamp` comparison of `RequiredL1` and `VerifiedRequiredL1` for each L2 block in the window:

1. **Steady state.** Derive through several L1 blocks, including L1 blocks that carry no batch data and span batches whose blocks share a source. Catches a key choice that differs (derivation source versus the block's own L1 origin).
2. **L1 reorg.** Trigger an L1 reorg with the existing `ReorgTriggered` DSL deep enough to unwind batches, then derive past it. Catches a truncation point that differs from the resume point.
3. **CL restart, EL kept.** Restart the kona verifier's CL only. Mirrors `TestNotTruncateDatabaseOnRestartWithExistingDatabase` (#22265).
4. **CL sync resume.** Mirrors `TestPreserveDatabaseOnCLResync`.
5. **EL resync.** Stop both and wipe the EL. Mirrors `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync`. Until the resume-from-tip follow-up on #23474 lands, kona-node clears its history here while op-node keeps and resumes from its tip, so this case documents the known difference and is expected to fail until then.
6. **Disabled.** A kona-node without a safedb path answers both RPCs with the same error class op-node does.

The existing `safeheaddb_elsync` and `safeheaddb_clsync` packages keep running under `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND=kona-node` (#23479); this package is the direct comparison.

## Done

- [ ] The package exists, runs in the acceptance matrix, and every scenario passes except 5, which is skipped with a pointer to the follow-up until it lands.
- [ ] A deliberate key mix-up (recording the block's own L1 origin) makes scenario 1 fail, confirming the comparison has teeth.
- [ ] Scenario 5 passes once the resume-from-tip follow-up lands, and the skip is removed.

topIssues.title: kona-node: safedb dashboard and alerts
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473. Depends on the metrics from #23478.

## Scope

Make the kona-node safedb observable on the devnets where kona-node runs, and page when it is unhealthy. The implementation lands in the k8s repo (Grafana dashboards and alert rules), following the existing k8s alert conventions (`team=protocol` routes to the protocol on-call; P3 and below is informational).

Dashboard, on the kona-node dashboard:

- safedb tip L1 block against the node's current L1 head, so lag is visible at a glance;
- safedb tip L2 block against local-safe;
- write, retry and truncation rates;
- a table of recent reset-below-tip warnings.

Alerts:

- safedb tip lagging the L1 head by more than a channel timeout for longer than 15 minutes while derivation is otherwise progressing (a gap is forming);
- any reset-below-tip warning (the condition that produced the hole in ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#402);
- write retries exhausted (the node stops, so this is a crash alert with a specific cause).

Threshold choices and a one-paragraph runbook per alert go into the alert annotations.

## Done

- [ ] Dashboard panels merged and visible for every kona-node on the kona-node sequencer devnet (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#283).
- [ ] The three alerts are merged, routed to protocol, and each has a runbook annotation.
- [ ] Each alert has fired at least once in a deliberate test (for example by stopping writes or restoring a stale snapshot) and the on-call received it.

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: keep upstream-clean packages compiling against the latest go-ethereum
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257.

The `opgeth-ratchet` check type-checks against the upstream go-ethereum version op-geth is based on (v1.17.2). Downstream modules that decouple ahead of #20266 move to the *latest* upstream go-ethereum, and Go's minimum version selection then compiles the monorepo's packages against that version too. They need at least v1.17.7 anyway: `op-service/sources` uses the backported `Header.BlockAccessListHash`. But the monorepo code they import has drifted from current upstream APIs, and nothing checks for it.

Against go-ethereum v1.17.7 and v1.17.8 (with the `op-core` transition code from #23525 removed; verified 2026-10-20 on develop@056afb5):

- `op-service/eth`: [`L1ChainConfigByChainID`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-service/eth/config.go#L16-L17) uses `params.HoleskyChainConfig`, which upstream removed. Fix: drop Holesky (shut down).
- `op-core/genesis`: [`storageRoot`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-core/genesis/block.go#L45) calls `StateDB.Commit(block, deleteEmpty, noStorageWiping)`; upstream's is `Commit(rules, block)`. Fix: compute the storage root with `trie.StackTrie` (same API in op-geth and v1.17.8); the existing `directStorageRoot` test helper is the oracle.
- `op-chain-ops/foundry`: the [`StateDB` interface](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-chain-ops/foundry/allocs.go#L35-L40) pins `DumpToCollector`'s return type, which upstream changed to `([]byte, error)`. Fix: take `*state.StateDB` and call `DumpToCollector` as a statement, which compiles against both. Reached by downstream modules through `op-chain-ops/genesis`.

## Gate

Extend `opgeth-ratchet` with a second pass: every package whose import closure contains no allowlisted package must also type-check against a pinned recent upstream go-ethereum release, with no allowlist. The set is derived, not curated, so a package that becomes upstream-clean is covered automatically. Bump the pin with upstream releases. Where a signature change can't be bridged in a shared package, move the code behind a seam (or into the transitional op-geth package) rather than allowlisting it.

Rebasing op-geth onto a newer upstream base isn't an option: the op-geth binary is end of life, and it would pull the drift into the fork-dependent code too.

## Done when

The three sites above compile against both op-geth and the latest upstream go-ethereum, and CI enforces it for every upstream-clean package.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: docs: publish the op-reth reference from gen-cli at v2.4.4 and retire the old CLI tree
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23102 (gen-cli); its diff shows that PR's commits until it merges.

The op-reth CLI reference is 73 pages under Node Operators › Reference, generated at v2.4.1 and three releases behind, with the same Logging and Display blocks reprinted on all 72 command pages and a 60-chain list on most of them, so a search for any common flag returns most of the tree (ethereum-optimism/solutions#1209). This replaces it with the first component on the generated, versioned reference the content guide specifies: 15 pages under `reference/op-reth/v2.4`, generated by gen-cli from the published `op-reth:v2.4.4` image in 13 seconds, with an index, one page per top-level command whose nested subcommands are headings, and a global-options page for the three sections every command repeated. The Reference tab now exists with the op-reth dropdown and its v2.4 version entry.

Effect on users: every old URL redirects. Nested subcommands land on the anchor of their heading (`db/checksum/mdbx` → `db#checksum-mdbx`), verified live with `mint dev` along with the root and overview redirects. The 69 older redirects that already pointed into the deleted tree are re-targeted so no redirect chains. The hand-written orientation page moves to Node Operators › Guides › Configuration ("Understanding the op-reth CLI"), since nothing under `reference/` is hand-written, and nine pages that linked into the old tree now link to the new one. The `op-reth node` page is 1,700 lines instead of the old tree's combined 17,700, and the chain list appears once, as a pointer to the superchain-registry. op-reth's flag catalog moves from three releases behind to current.

Effect on maintainers: `gen-op-reth-cli` is deleted; gen-cli regenerates this line with `--component op-reth --tag <tag> --image auto`, and `--check` verifies it. The nav, redirect, reference and link-policy lints pass on this branch with its own lint scripts (#23102 now carries the nav-lint change that understands `dropdowns`/`versions`, identical to #23091's, so this no longer waits on #23091). Until the tag-triggered regeneration job lands (ethereum-optimism/solutions#1518, Phase 2.2), a new op-reth release is regenerated by hand; the old tree had no working automation either (the README described one that was never registered), so this gap is not new.

Review: the deletion-reviewer agent swept the whole repository for references to the deleted URLs, nav group and generator, and verified one redirect per deleted URL, every anchored destination against the target page's headings, no chains, and no other generator or asset referencing the old tree. It found one dead link in `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md` step 9 of the reth-bump procedure (fixed), three descriptions that still said the reference was imported from the source tree or that subcommands get their own pages (fixed), and the nav-lint dependency above (resolved by carrying the change in #23102). No findings dismissed.

Redirect destinations name the `v2.4` line. When a new minor line ships and becomes the default, those redirects still resolve but land on v2.4; retargeting them is a one-line job for the regeneration workflow and is tracked with the versioning work rather than done here.

Refs ethereum-optimism/solutions#1518 (Phase 2, first migration); closes the collapse asked for in ethereum-optimism/solutions#1209. Depends on #23102 and #23091.

topPRs.title: op-reth!: demonstrate optimistic parallel execution PoC
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
This PoC explores reducing op-reth execution latency by speculating on independent transactions while preserving canonical transaction order, state, receipts, fees, and SDM settlement. It covers Engine validation, historical execution, forced transactions, pool sequencing, and subblock continuation. **Sequential execution remains the default; parallel and rolling execution are opt-in.**

The [PoC write-up](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/POC.md) covers the high-level architecture, low-level decisions, results, and production gates. The [README](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/README.md) documents configuration and reproduction commands.

The central choice is bounded speculation against immutable snapshots of **committed state only**. One coordinator validates dependencies and commits in order; stale or failed attempts execute once canonically. This avoids speculative worker-to-worker dependencies and cascading rollback. Independent worker-local readers remove coordinator read messages, and optional rolling scheduling overlaps ordered commit with further execution. Broker windows remain the compatibility fallback.

Protocol fee credits are settled in order without manufacturing dependencies between otherwise independent transactions. SDM observation is transaction-local; refund evaluation and policy updates remain ordered and commit-only. The authoritative selector controls inclusion, with `on_commit` before its next `next()`. Resource limits cover outstanding attempts, speculative gas, dependencies, outputs, and retained snapshot versions. Shared worker permits, generation checks, and reader-teardown barriers govern cancellation and competing operations.

| Synthetic comparison | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Final rolling vs sequential: independent compute | 3.1x at 4 workers; 4.4x at 8 |
| Final rolling vs sequential: stock BN254 pairings | 3.7x at 4 workers; 6.3x at 8 |
| Independent readers vs broker windows: storage | 5-6x at 4 workers |
| Rolling vs direct windows | 14-35% lower storage latency; 13% lower expensive-policy latency at 4 workers |

These are separate local in-memory experiments using an optimized test profile; their ratios are not cumulative. Cheap storage often remains faster sequentially. Contention, read amplification, retained snapshots, serial policy work, and tail latency limit the gains. No production database or end-to-end replay speedup is claimed. See the [performance report and raw data](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/benchmarks/session-summary.md).

This draft depends on [ethereum-optimism/reth#10](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/pull/10). Before production: land reviewed source hooks; independently review and fuzz consensus-sensitive paths; replay representative chain ranges against known roots; measure release-build latency, memory, database I/O, and competing builds; integrate the real SDM policy; and complete shadow soak and canary rollout. Upstream borrowed/Arc configuration wrappers currently retain broker reads, and opaque Engine precompile-cache wrappers require canonical precompile fallback. Both remain documented compatibility limitations.

BREAKING CHANGE: Downstream Rust integrations constructing `OpBlockExecutionCtx` must supply `parallel_candidates` (empty for sequential execution) or use `..Default::default()`. Runtime-bearing executor factories and `OpExecutorBuilder` require explicit cloning instead of `Copy`; custom `OpTxEnv` implementations need `Clone`; generic `OpBlockExecutor` users must carry its `Evm` bound. Construct `OpHandler` with `OpHandler::new()` instead of external struct literals. No Engine API wire or database migration is introduced.

Validation: 603 affected execution/integration/txpool/CLI tests pass (3 skipped), including the rebased txpool affordability changes. The saved 121-configuration rolling benchmark checks output parity. Formatting, scoped Clippy with warnings denied, rustdoc, affected `no_std` builds, and the upstream-mirror check pass.

Rust correctness, deletion/write-preservation, and reth dependency/mirror reviews completed. Provider-failure propagation has regression coverage through actual EVM errors and cancellation races. The reth wrapper limitation above remains an open production follow-up. Full workspace `just lint` is blocked in the unchanged `gmp-mpfr-sys` dependency by missing `m4`; scoped checks are reported separately above.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: prove below-head interop references with log-commitment batches
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
PR 2 lets the SP1 consolidation check a message to a block below the initiating chain's local safe head against a log-commitment entry instead of that block's receipts. This PR makes the proposer (and the executor test tool) use it, so referencing many large blocks no longer makes one timestamp unprovable.

The proposer scans a game's messages at proof time and picks one path per game: receipts when every request's bound fits, otherwise the table path, where it proves each referenced block once in batches before any consolidation and attaches the covering batch proofs to each request. Requests over the PGU budget, the witness cap, or 4 GiB of stdin are refused, and on the table path the proposer applies these checks to the scan-fixed part of each request before any batch request. `LOG_PATH=receipts` turns the table path off.

The proposer now needs `<vkey>.log.bin.gz` next to the other two artifacts, so prestates published before the log program (`v0.0.1`, `v0.0.2-rc.1`) cannot be loaded. New settings: `LOG_PATH`, `LOG_PROOF_STRATEGY`, `LOG_CYCLE_LIMIT`, `LOG_GAS_LIMIT` (10¹¹).

Testing: unit tests for the scan, path choice, batching, retries, and request checks; ELF-gated tests that pin each estimator at or above measured PGU; interop acceptance with a below-head reference (Kona, SP1 native core, full ELF); a ZK acceptance test on the table path with the mock provider. The pre-check is unit-tested, but no test fails on the baseline at its call site. Gaps: a replaced head's cost is not calibrated (no state in the fixture), executor memory at the caps is not yet measured on Linux, the canary still takes the receipts path (proofs-team#30), and there is no persistent batch cache (proofs-team#31).

topPRs.title: kona-node,kona-engine!: execute engine commands through one owner
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
An unsafe backlog or execution RPC failure can trap reset control, and derivation currently has to infer success from engine callbacks. Give execution mutations and resets one owner with bounded admission, epoch checks, acknowledged outcomes and state publication before replies. This removes the task heap, forwarding operation clients and callback state machine while keeping the independent kona-node connected to an external execution client.

Derived rejection now uses the L1 inclusion timestamp, distinguishes INVALID from temporary statuses, and performs the deposits-only replacement only where required. Pending span progress stays separate from completed safe/finalized progress; finality records carry the actual accepted block hash and inclusion source. Sequencer retries retain the retrieved payload, and full engine admission leaves networking responsive.

Stacked on #23488. The tracked [implementation plan](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/kona-refactor-05-engine-owner/docs/ai/kona-node-pr-plan.md) records scope and the remaining stack. Read-only RPC and sequencer-admin forwarding remain for their planned follow-ups; bootstrap policy and the canonical reset walk are preserved. The force-inclusion verifier receives one real startup block, then derives through the outage without L2 peers or further unsafe injection; idle-start bootstrap remains PR10.

Closes #22681. Its forced-inclusion regression is preserved by #23494 without a verifier startup payload primer; #23495 validates the recovered safe/finalized chain with engine-owned finality.

BREAKING CHANGE: replaces public Engine/task/error-severity wrappers and operation forwarding clients with ordinary kona-engine operations and kona-node-service EngineHandle. Downstream composition constructs EngineActor together with its handle; derived imports use ImportMode, EngineState includes phase/epoch/pending-safe, and producers carry captured context instead of sending raw operation messages.

Local validation: 321 offline tests, 115 focused tests, full workspace Rust lint, full repository Go lint, and a fresh default node build pass. The real short-window force-inclusion regression passes with a Kona sequencer and isolated Kona verifier. Four existing reorg subcases across both presets and both Kona restart tests also pass. Independent Rust/protocol, Go and deletion/API reviews completed; all actionable findings were fixed.
